'''Southwestern Bontoc''' (Southwestern Bontok) is a variety of the [[Bontoc language]] of the [[Philippines]]. This language is a [[Endangered language|moribund language]], with only 2,470 speakers left in 2007.<ref name=":0">[[ethnologue:vbk|Southwestern Bontok]] at ''[[Ethnologue]]''. {{Subscription required}}</ref>

== Distribution and dialects ==
[[Ethnologue]] reports the following locations for Southwestern Bontok:

[[Cordillera Administrative Region]]: [[Mountain Province]]: [[Bontoc, Mountain Province|Bontoc Municipality]]: Alab, Balili, Gonogon and some villages near [[Chico River (Philippines)|Chico River Valley]] and the southwest of [[Bontoc, Mountain Province|Bontoc Municipality]].<ref name=":0" />

[[Ethnologue]] identifies Ina-ab, Binalili and Ginonogon as dialects of Southwestern Bontok.<ref name=":0" />

== Similarities ==
[[Ethnologue]] reports the language is similar to 4 other [[Bontoc language]]s: [[Central Bontok language|Central Bontok]], [[North Bontok language|North Bontok]], [[South Bontoc language|Southern Bontok]] and [[East Bontoc language|Eastern Bontok]].

== Death of the language ==
This language is a moribund language, which means that only a few people speak it and if the speakers of the language continue to speak [[Tagalog language|Tagalog]] or [[English language|English]] to their sons and not speak their own mother tongue, the language will not be passed down to newer generations, eventually becoming a "[[Extinct language|dead language]]". Many of the speakers have shifted to [[Ilocano language|Ilokano]]. Many of the speakers can also speak [[Central Bontok language|Central Bontok]] and [[Kankanaey language|Kankanaey]] as their second language.<ref name=":0" />
